chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the wheat and the barley, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If they are equal, there is no problem.' He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about the wheat and the flour, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If they are equal, there is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging wheat for barley or flour in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the application of the 'like-for-like' (mithl bi mithl) principle in barter transactions, specifically addressing the exchange of wheat with barley or flour. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise measurement and equivalence to prevent riba (usury) in commodity trades, ensuring that the physical attributes of the goods are comparable when exchanged directly.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the wheat and the barley, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If they are equated, so there is no problem’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the wheat and the flour, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When they are equated, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “

I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about wheat and barley. He (the Imam) said, ‘If they are of equal measures it is not harmful.’ He (the narrator) has said, ‘I asked him (the Imam) about flour and wheat. He (the Imam) said, ‘If they are of equal measures it is not harmful.’”
